posture_tips: Lie with your eyes under the bar, feet planted, and grip just wider than shoulder width so forearms are vertical at the bottom.
Pinch your shoulder blades down and back and keep a slight arch, with glutes, upper back and head on the bench.
Lower the bar in 2-3 seconds to your lower chest, touch without bouncing, then press up and slightly back over your shoulders.
Don't flare your elbows to 90 degrees; keep them about 45-70 degrees from your torso on the way down.
Use safety arms or a spotter whenever you train close to failure.
squeeze_cue: Squeeze your chest as if trying to bend the bar into a U and bring your biceps toward each other as you press up.

posture_tips: Set the bench to 30-45 degrees and lie down with the bar roughly over your eyes, feet flat on the floor.
Keep your shoulder blades pulled back and chest up without lifting your glutes off the seat.
Lower the bar in 2-3 seconds to just below your collarbones, pause lightly, then press straight up over your shoulders.
Don't set the incline too steep, or it turns into a shoulder press.
Unrack and rerack the bar with locked-out arms, never with bent elbows.
squeeze_cue: Press up and feel your upper chest pull your arms in toward your chin, as if hugging the bar toward your collarbones.

posture_tips: Hook your feet securely under the rollers before lying back, with your eyes under the bar.
Keep your shoulder blades squeezed together and your head on the bench throughout.
Lower the bar in 2-3 seconds to your lower chest, then press up until your arms are straight without slamming into lockout.
Don't bounce the bar off your sternum to get it moving.
Get a spotter to hand off and rerack: the decline angle makes it hard to rack the bar alone.
squeeze_cue: Drive the bar up and squeeze your lower chest as if pressing your upper arms down and in toward your ribs.

posture_tips: Sit on a 30-45 degree incline with dumbbells on your thighs and kick them up with your knees as you lie back.
Keep your chest up, shoulder blades pinned back, and wrists straight, stacked directly over your elbows.
Lower in 2-3 seconds until the dumbbells are beside your upper chest, then press up, bringing them slightly together at the top.
Don't clank the dumbbells together or lose tension at the top.
When done, bring the dumbbells to your chest and sit up with them on your thighs instead of dropping them.
squeeze_cue: As you press, squeeze your upper chest to bring your biceps up and in toward your chin, as if closing a book over your face.

name_es: Press de banca con mancuernas (inclinado, agarre neutro)
posture_tips: Lie on a 30-45 degree incline with palms facing each other and the dumbbells over your upper chest.
Keep your elbows about 30 degrees from your torso and forearms vertical throughout the rep.
Lower in 2-3 seconds until the dumbbells brush the sides of your chest, then press up under control.
Don't rotate your wrists mid-rep; keep your palms facing each other the whole time.
Pick a weight you can control on the way down; if the dumbbells drift or wobble, go lighter.
squeeze_cue: Press the handles up and toward each other, squeezing your upper chest as if trying to make your inner elbows touch.

name_es: Press de banca con barra (agarre cerrado)
posture_tips: Grip the bar with hands about shoulder-width apart, no narrower, with your eyes under the bar.
Keep your elbows tucked close to your body and wrists stacked over your forearms.
Lower the bar in 2 seconds to your lower chest, then press up until your elbows fully lock out.
Don't bring your hands too close: it loads your wrists without hitting the triceps any harder.
Set safety pins just below chest height if you train without a spotter.
squeeze_cue: Lock out by squeezing the back of your arms hard, as if trying to snap the bar in half by pushing your hands apart.

name_es: Press de banca con barra (declinado, agarre cerrado)
posture_tips: Lock your feet under the decline bench rollers and grip the bar about shoulder-width apart.
Keep your elbows close to your torso and your head on the bench for the whole set.
Lower the bar in 2 seconds to your lower chest, then press up until your elbows are fully extended.
Don't let your elbows flare out as you press.
Train with a spotter who can help you unrack and rerack the bar in this position.
squeeze_cue: At lockout, squeeze your triceps hard and feel your elbows straighten fully, as if pushing the bar through the ceiling.

name_es: Press de pecho en máquina de discos (agarre ancho)
posture_tips: Adjust the seat so the wide handles line up with your mid-chest when you sit down.
Keep your back and head against the pad with your shoulder blades pinned back.
Press forward without locking your elbows, then take 2-3 seconds to return until you feel a stretch across your chest.
Don't let your shoulders roll off the pad at the end of the press.
Load and unload plates evenly on both sides of the machine.
squeeze_cue: Push the handles forward and squeeze your chest as if trying to make your biceps touch in front of you.

name_es: Press de pecho en máquina (agarre ancho)
posture_tips: Set the seat height so the wide handles sit level with your mid-chest.
Keep your back firmly against the pad, chest up, and shoulder blades squeezed back.
Press until your arms are almost straight, then take 2-3 seconds to return until your hands reach chest level.
Don't let the weight stack touch down between reps; keep constant tension.
Make sure the weight pin is fully inserted before you start the set.
squeeze_cue: Squeeze your chest as you push, as if trying to make your biceps touch at the end of the press.

posture_tips: Set the pulleys at chest height, grab the handles, and step forward into a staggered stance.
Keep a slight, fixed bend in your elbows and your torso steady, with no rocking.
Hug your hands together in front of your chest in a wide arc, hold 1 second, then take 2-3 seconds to return to a stretch.
Don't turn the fly into a press by bending and straightening your elbows.
Don't let your arms travel behind your body line if you feel strain in the shoulder.
squeeze_cue: Bring your hands together as if hugging a big tree and squeeze your chest hard, pressing your biceps toward each other.

name_es: Aperturas en polea (de arriba hacia abajo)
posture_tips: Set the pulleys at the highest position and stagger your feet for a stable base.
Lean your torso slightly forward and keep your chest open and shoulders down.
Sweep your hands down and in to hip height, hold 1 second, then let them rise back over 2-3 seconds.
Don't round your shoulders forward as your hands come together.
Use a weight that lets you control the return without the cables yanking your arms back.
squeeze_cue: Sweep down and squeeze your lower chest as if pressing your biceps into your ribs and your hands toward your belt buckle.

posture_tips: Secure your feet on the decline bench and press the dumbbells over your chest, palms facing in.
Keep a slight, fixed bend in your elbows for the entire set.
Open your arms in a 2-3 second arc until you feel a chest stretch, then bring them back together over your sternum.
Don't lower the dumbbells below the level of the bench.
Start light: dumbbells are harder to control on a decline.
squeeze_cue: Close the arc as if hugging a barrel and squeeze your lower chest, bringing your inner arms toward each other.

posture_tips: Support yourself on narrow parallel bars with arms locked out and body upright.
Keep your torso tall and elbows pointing back, tucked close to your sides.
Lower in 2 seconds until your elbows reach about 90 degrees, then press back up to full extension.
Don't let your shoulders shrug up toward your ears at the bottom.
Only go as deep as you can control without discomfort at the front of the shoulder.
squeeze_cue: Push the bars down toward the floor and squeeze your triceps hard at the top until your elbows are fully locked.

name_es: Press de banca en máquina Smith
posture_tips: Position the bench so the bar comes down right on your lower chest.
Pinch your shoulder blades together and plant your feet firmly on the floor.
Twist to unrack, lower in 2-3 seconds to your chest, and press straight up without bouncing.
Don't set the bench too far up or back: the bar should land on your chest, not your neck.
Set the Smith machine safety stops just above chest height before you start.
squeeze_cue: Press up and squeeze your chest as if trying to drag your hands toward each other along the bar.

name_es: Press de banca en máquina Smith (inclinado)
posture_tips: Position the incline bench so the bar travels down to your upper chest.
Keep your shoulder blades retracted and your glutes on the seat.
Lower the bar in 2-3 seconds until it touches just below your collarbones, then press with steady force.
Don't lift your back off the bench to move more weight.
Rotate the hooks to lock the bar in as soon as you finish your last rep.
squeeze_cue: As you press, squeeze your upper chest as if pulling your hands together on the bar toward your chin.

posture_tips: Sit with dumbbells on your thighs and kick them to your chest with your knees as you lie back.
Keep your shoulder blades together and forearms vertical over your elbows.
Lower in 2-3 seconds to the sides of your chest, then press up in a slight arc toward the middle.
Don't let the dumbbells drift toward your head or feet as you lower them.
If you fail a rep, bring the dumbbells to your chest and sit up instead of dropping them out wide.
squeeze_cue: Press up and squeeze your chest as if trying to make your biceps touch at the top.

posture_tips: Lock your feet on the decline bench with the dumbbells resting on your chest before lying back.
Keep your head on the bench and wrists firm, stacked over your elbows.
Lower in 2-3 seconds toward your lower chest, then press until your arms are nearly straight.
Don't over-arch your back to grind the weight up.
Have a partner hand you the dumbbells if getting them into position on the decline is awkward.
squeeze_cue: Press up and in, squeezing your lower chest as if trying to make your elbows meet over your stomach.

posture_tips: Adjust the seat so the handles line up with your upper chest.
Keep your back and head against the pad, shoulder blades back, and chest open.
Press up and forward without locking your elbows, then take 2-3 seconds to return to the start.
Don't shrug your shoulders toward your ears as you press.
Check that the seat is locked in place before loading any weight.
squeeze_cue: Push up and in, squeezing your upper chest just below your collarbones as if bringing your biceps toward your chin.

name_es: Press de pecho en máquina de discos (inclinado)
posture_tips: Sit with the handles at upper-chest height and your feet flat on the floor.
Keep your shoulder blades together and your back pressed into the pad.
Press the machine arms up, then lower in 2-3 seconds until you feel a stretch across your upper chest.
Don't lower so fast that the plates crash at the bottom of the rep.
Strip plates evenly from both sides so the machine doesn't tip out of balance.
squeeze_cue: At the top, squeeze your upper chest as if trying to make your biceps touch in front of your face.

posture_tips: Lie on a flat bench with the dumbbells over your chest and palms facing each other.
Keep a slight, fixed bend in your elbows and your shoulder blades pinned together.
Open your arms in a 2-3 second arc to chest level, then close them as if hugging a tree.
Don't go so heavy that you have to bend your elbows and turn it into a press.
Don't let your arms drop below shoulder level.
squeeze_cue: Lead the arc with your inner arms and squeeze your chest as if trying to make your biceps kiss at the top.

posture_tips: Set the bench to a low incline of about 30 degrees and press the dumbbells up over your upper chest.
Keep your chest up and a slight, constant bend in your elbows.
Open your arms in 2-3 seconds until you feel a stretch, then arc them back together over your collarbones.
Don't let the dumbbells drift back toward your head instead of out to the sides.
Take extra care on the lowering phase; that's where the shoulder is most exposed.
squeeze_cue: Close the arc up and in, squeezing your upper chest as if hugging a barrel against your collarbones.

name_es: Aperturas en polea (de abajo hacia arriba)
posture_tips: Set the pulleys at the lowest position, grab the handles, and step forward between them.
Keep your torso upright, chest open, and elbows slightly bent.
Sweep your hands up in an arc to chin height, hold 1 second, then lower over 2-3 seconds.
Don't pull with your biceps or shrug your shoulders on the way up.
Grab and release the handles with the stack at rest so you don't get pulled off balance.
squeeze_cue: Scoop up and in, squeezing your upper chest as if lifting your biceps to touch in front of your chin.

posture_tips: Adjust the seat so the handles are at chest height with your elbows nearly straight.
Keep your back against the pad and shoulder blades together for the whole set.
Bring the handles together in front of your chest, squeeze for a second, and open over 2-3 seconds.
Don't let your arms swing too far back on the stretch when the weight is heavy.
Set the machine's range-of-motion stop to limit how far back your arms go if needed.
squeeze_cue: Drive with your inner arms, not your hands, and squeeze your chest as if trying to make your biceps touch.

posture_tips: Place your hands slightly wider than your shoulders and extend your legs into a plank.
Keep a straight line from head to heels by squeezing your glutes and abs.
Lower in 2 seconds until your chest nearly touches the floor, then push back up to straight arms.
Don't let your hips sag or pike up.
If you lose body position, drop to your knees or elevate your hands to finish the set.
squeeze_cue: Push the floor away and squeeze your chest as if trying to drag your hands toward each other.

posture_tips: Place your hands on a sturdy bench or box, slightly wider than your shoulders.
Keep your body straight as a board with your abs and glutes braced.
Lower in 2 seconds until your chest reaches the edge of the bench, then push back up to straight arms.
Don't let your head reach the bench before your chest does.
Make sure the bench or box can't slide before you put weight on it.
squeeze_cue: Push the bench away and squeeze your chest as if trying to pull your hands together along its edge.

posture_tips: Put your feet on a bench and your hands on the floor, slightly wider than your shoulders.
Brace your abs and glutes so your lower back doesn't sag.
Lower in 2 seconds until your chest nearly touches the floor in front of your hands, then push back up.
Don't pike your hips up to shorten the range of motion.
Start with your feet only slightly elevated and raise them once your technique is solid.
squeeze_cue: Push up and squeeze your upper chest as if drawing your hands toward each other and up toward your chin.

posture_tips: Place your hands under your shoulders or slightly narrower, fingers pointing forward.
Keep your elbows tucked to your ribs and your body in a straight line.
Lower in 2 seconds until your chest brushes your hands, then push up by straightening your elbows.
Don't let your elbows flare out to the sides on the way down.
If your wrists feel loaded, widen your hands a little or use push-up handles.
squeeze_cue: Push the floor away and squeeze the back of your arms hard as your elbows lock out at the top.

posture_tips: Mount the parallel bars with arms locked out and legs slightly behind you.
Lean your torso slightly forward and keep your shoulders down, away from your ears.
Lower in 2-3 seconds until your shoulders are level with your elbows, then press back to the top.
Don't swing your legs to kip your way up.
Shorten the range or use assistance if you can't control the bottom position.
squeeze_cue: Press up and squeeze your chest as if trying to pull the two bars toward each other.

posture_tips: Select the counterweight, kneel on the pad, and grip the bars with your arms locked out.
Keep your torso slightly forward and your shoulders down and back.
Lower in 2-3 seconds until your elbows reach about 90 degrees, then press to full extension.
Remember more counterweight means more help; don't add it just to rep faster.
Step on and off the platform carefully, always holding onto the handles.
squeeze_cue: Press down and squeeze your chest and triceps as if trying to pull the handles in toward your hips.

posture_tips: Sit on a bench with a near-vertical back pad and kick the dumbbells up to shoulder height.
Keep your back on the pad, core braced, and wrists stacked over your elbows.
Press in a slight arc until the dumbbells nearly touch overhead, then take 2-3 seconds to lower to ear level.
Don't arch your lower back to peel off the pad.
Get the dumbbells to your shoulders by resting them on your knees first.
squeeze_cue: Drive up and feel the front of your shoulders work, as if pushing the ceiling away while your biceps close toward your ears.

name_es: Press de hombros con mancuernas (agarre neutro)
posture_tips: Hold the dumbbells at shoulder height with your palms facing each other.
Keep your elbows in front of your body and your torso tight, without leaning back.
Press straight overhead, then take 2-3 seconds to lower to about chin level.
Don't flare your elbows out; with a neutral grip they should stay in front.
Use a bench with back support if you find yourself swaying as you press.
squeeze_cue: Press straight up and feel the front of your shoulders lift, as if punching both fists through the ceiling.

name_es: Press de hombros en máquina (agarre neutro)
posture_tips: Adjust the seat so the neutral handles sit at shoulder height.
Keep your back and head on the pad with your elbows slightly in front of your body.
Press up without locking your elbows, then take 2-3 seconds to lower to shoulder height.
Don't let the weight stack rest between reps.
Check the seat height: starting too low puts your shoulder in a strained position.
squeeze_cue: Drive the handles up and squeeze the front of your shoulders, as if lifting the ceiling with your fists.

name_es: Press de hombros en máquina (agarre ancho)
posture_tips: Sit with the wide handles at ear height and your feet planted on the floor.
Keep your back against the pad, wrists straight, and elbows under your hands.
Press until your arms are nearly straight, then take 2-3 seconds to lower to the start.
Don't shrug your shoulders up toward your ears as you press.
Secure the weight pin and seat adjustment before every set.
squeeze_cue: Push up and feel the top of your shoulders squeeze, as if pressing your upper arms toward your ears.

name_es: Press de hombros en máquina de discos (agarre ancho)
posture_tips: Set the seat so you start with the wide handles just above your shoulders.
Keep your back and head on the pad and your core engaged.
Press the machine arms up, then take 2-3 seconds to lower until your hands are just above shoulder height.
Don't arch your lower back to grind out the last reps.
Load plates evenly on both sides and strip them when you're done.
squeeze_cue: Drive the handles up and squeeze your shoulders as if trying to bring your biceps to your ears at the top.

posture_tips: Adjust the seat so the machine's pivot lines up with your shoulder joints.
Rest your chest or back against the pad and keep your shoulders down.
Raise your arms out to shoulder height in about 1 second, pause briefly, then lower over 2-3 seconds.
Don't shrug with your traps to get extra height.
Choose a weight you can lower under control without the plates slamming down.
squeeze_cue: Push the pads out with your elbows and feel the side of your shoulder lift, as if pushing two walls apart.

posture_tips: Stand with feet hip-width apart and the dumbbells just in front of your thighs.
Lean slightly forward and keep a soft bend in your elbows, with elbows leading the hands.
Raise the dumbbells out to shoulder height, then take 2-3 seconds to lower them.
Don't swing your body to fling the dumbbells up.
Don't raise your hands above shoulder height if you feel pinching or discomfort.
squeeze_cue: Lead with your elbows and feel the side of your shoulder lift the weight, as if reaching your hands out to the walls.

name_es: Elevaciones en Y con mancuernas (banco inclinado)
posture_tips: Lie face down on a steep incline bench, dumbbells hanging and thumbs pointing up.
Keep your chest on the bench and your neck neutral throughout.
Raise your arms in a Y shape to ear height, hold 1 second, then lower over 2-3 seconds.
Don't shrug toward your ears or lift your chest off the bench.
Use light dumbbells: form breaks down quickly on this one when the load is too heavy.
squeeze_cue: Reach long into the Y and feel the side and back of your shoulders lift, as if pushing your thumbs up toward the ceiling.

posture_tips: Unrack the bar at collarbone height with a grip slightly wider than your shoulders and elbows slightly in front.
Squeeze your glutes and abs to keep your ribs down and your spine neutral.
Press the bar straight up, push your head through at the top, and lower to your collarbones in 2 seconds.
Don't lean back so far that it becomes an incline press.
Set the rack hooks at chest height so you can unrack and rerack the bar safely.
squeeze_cue: Drive the bar up and squeeze your shoulders as if trying to bend the bar overhead while your biceps finish by your ears.

posture_tips: Sit on an upright bench under the racked bar with your feet planted and grip just outside shoulder width.
Keep your back against the pad, ribs down, and head neutral.
Lower the bar in front of your face to chin level in 2 seconds, then press until your arms are straight.
Don't lower the bar behind your neck.
Set the hooks so you can unrack the bar without fully extending your arms to reach it.
squeeze_cue: Press up and feel the front of your shoulders squeeze, as if pushing the ceiling away with the bar.

name_es: Press de hombros en máquina Smith (sentado)
posture_tips: Set an upright bench so the bar travels just in front of your face.
Keep your back on the pad and your wrists straight over your elbows.
Unrack the bar, lower it to your chin in 2-3 seconds, and press up without locking out hard.
Don't jut your head forward toward the bar as you lower it.
Set the Smith machine safety stops at shoulder height.
squeeze_cue: Drive the bar up and squeeze the front of your shoulders, as if trying to pull your hands together on the bar.

name_es: Press de hombros con mancuernas (de pie)
posture_tips: Stand with feet hip-width apart and the dumbbells resting at your shoulders.
Brace your abs and squeeze your glutes so your lower back doesn't arch.
Press the dumbbells overhead, then take 2-3 seconds to lower to ear level.
Don't drive the weight with your legs unless you're doing a deliberate push press.
Go lighter than the seated version: standing demands more stability.
squeeze_cue: Push up and feel your shoulders lift the weight, as if punching both fists straight through the ceiling.

posture_tips: Sit with the dumbbells in front of your chin and palms facing you.
Keep your back on the pad and your elbows in front at the start.
Rotate your palms forward as you press up, then reverse the rotation over 2-3 seconds as you lower.
Don't split the rotation and the press into two separate movements.
Use less weight than on a standard press so you can control the rotation.
squeeze_cue: As your palms turn out, feel the front and side of your shoulders squeeze, as if opening a door on each side of your head.

posture_tips: Hold the end of the bar at shoulder height in one hand with the opposite foot forward.
Keep your trunk tight and your shoulders square to the front, without twisting.
Press the bar up and forward to full arm extension, then take 2 seconds to lower it to your shoulder.
Don't lean away to the opposite side to press the bar.
Anchor the fixed end of the bar in a landmine unit or a secure corner.
squeeze_cue: Punch the bar up and across, squeezing your upper chest and front shoulder as if reaching to shake a tall person's hand.

posture_tips: Sit on the end of a bench with the dumbbells at your sides and feet flat.
Keep your torso tall and your shoulders down, away from your ears.
Raise your arms out to shoulder height in about 1 second, pause briefly, then lower over 2-3 seconds.
Don't rotate the dumbbells thumb-down as if pouring a jug of water.
Use a light weight that lets you pause briefly at the top.
squeeze_cue: Lead with your elbows and feel the side of your shoulder do the lifting, as if pushing your hands out to the walls.

name_es: Elevaciones laterales en polea (a una mano)
posture_tips: Set the pulley low and grab the handle with the hand farthest from the machine.
Keep your torso steady by holding the machine with your free hand.
Raise your arm out to shoulder height, pause briefly, then lower over 2-3 seconds while resisting the cable.
Don't lean your trunk to cheat extra range of motion.
Start light: the cable keeps tension on the muscle through the whole rep.
squeeze_cue: Lead with your elbow and feel the side of your shoulder lift, as if pushing your hand far out to the wall.

posture_tips: Stand with the dumbbells in front of your thighs and your palms facing you.
Keep your core braced and your elbows slightly bent.
Raise the dumbbells in front of you to shoulder height, then take 2-3 seconds to lower them.
Don't lean back to heave the weight up.
Stop at eye level; going higher adds no useful work.
squeeze_cue: Lift with the front of your shoulders, as if reaching your hands forward to place the weights on a high shelf.

posture_tips: Stand facing away from a low pulley with the rope or bar between your legs.
Keep your torso upright and your arms nearly straight.
Raise the handle in front of you to shoulder height, then take 2-3 seconds to lower while resisting the cable.
Don't let the cable pull you backward on the way down.
Take a wide enough stance to stay balanced against the cable's pull.
squeeze_cue: Raise the handle with the front of your shoulders, as if reaching forward to hand something to someone in front of you.

posture_tips: Hinge at the hips with a flat back and let the dumbbells hang under your chest.
Keep your spine neutral and your neck in line with your torso.
Raise your arms out wide with a slight elbow bend, pause at the top, then lower over 2-3 seconds.
Don't over-squeeze your shoulder blades; the movement should come from the shoulder.
If keeping your back flat is hard, rest your forehead on an incline bench.
squeeze_cue: Sweep your arms out wide and feel the back of your shoulders squeeze, as if throwing the dumbbells to the side walls.

posture_tips: Lie face down on an incline bench with the dumbbells hanging and palms facing each other.
Keep your chest glued to the bench and your chin neutral.
Raise your arms out wide to shoulder level, pause 1 second, then lower over 2-3 seconds.
Don't lift your chest off the bench to build momentum.
Use light dumbbells and put control ahead of load.
squeeze_cue: Reach your hands out wide and feel the back of your shoulders work, as if spreading giant wings.

posture_tips: Set the pulleys at shoulder height and cross the cables, holding each with the opposite hand.
Keep your arms nearly straight and your chest open.
Pull your arms back and out until they line up with your body, pause, then return over 2-3 seconds.
Don't bend your elbows and turn it into a row.
Take a stable step back before you start so you don't lose your balance.
squeeze_cue: Pull your hands out to the side walls and squeeze the back of your shoulders, as if stretching a wide rubber band.

posture_tips: Sit facing the pad with the handles at shoulder height and arms nearly straight.
Keep your chest on the pad and your shoulders down for the whole set.
Sweep your arms back in an arc to your body line, pause 1 second, then return over 2-3 seconds.
Don't pull with your traps by shrugging your shoulders.
Set the machine arms to the reverse position before you sit down.
squeeze_cue: Push the handles back with the backs of your hands and squeeze the rear of your shoulders, as if opening heavy curtains.

posture_tips: Set the pulley at face height or slightly higher and grip the rope with palms facing down.
Keep your torso tall and stable, without leaning back.
Pull the rope to your face, split your hands apart and rotate out, hold 1 second, then return over 2 seconds.
Don't pull to your chest like a row; your hands should finish by your ears.
Use a moderate weight that lets you control the final rotation.
squeeze_cue: Pull the rope apart and finish like a double-biceps pose, squeezing the back of your shoulders and between your shoulder blades.

posture_tips: Hold the band in front of your chest, arms straight and hands shoulder-width apart.
Keep your ribs down and your shoulders away from your ears.
Pull your hands apart until the band touches your chest, hold 1 second, then return slowly without losing tension.
Don't bend your elbows to make it easier.
Inspect the band before use and throw it out if it has cracks or nicks.
squeeze_cue: Pull the band apart and squeeze the back of your shoulders, as if trying to stretch the band from wall to wall.

posture_tips: Hold the bar in front of your thighs with hands slightly wider than shoulder width.
Keep your torso upright and the bar close to your body.
Lead with your elbows to lift the bar to your lower chest, pause briefly, then lower over 2-3 seconds.
Don't pull the bar all the way to your chin with a narrow grip.
Stop at chest height if you feel discomfort at the top of your shoulder.
squeeze_cue: Drive your elbows up and out and feel the side of your shoulders lift, as if pulling the bar apart.

posture_tips: Face a low pulley with a straight bar or rope, gripping slightly wider than your shoulders.
Keep your back straight and your shoulders relaxed at the start.
Raise your elbows out to shoulder height, pause briefly, then lower over 2-3 seconds while resisting the cable.
Don't lift your wrists higher than your elbows.
Use a moderate weight; the cable shouldn't pull you forward.
squeeze_cue: Lift your elbows up and out to the sides and squeeze the side of your shoulders, as if trying to touch the walls with them.

posture_tips: Place your hands and feet on the floor and lift your hips into an inverted V.
Keep your hips high and your back straight throughout.
Lower in 2 seconds so your head moves toward the floor just in front of your hands, then push back up.
Don't drop your hips and turn it into a regular push-up.
Lower slowly and don't put any weight on your head at the bottom.
squeeze_cue: Push the floor away and feel your shoulders squeeze, as if pressing your body up toward the ceiling through your hands.
